novelty_points.claim: 提出了一种新的图表示学习模型——GSAERU，用于大规模时序图数据上的节点表征学习。
novelty_points.claim_en: Proposed a new graph representation learning model - GSAERU, for node representation learning on large-scale sequential graphs.
technical_features: 通过图摘要技术将原图映射到固定规模的新图中，解决了GNN模型输出无法直接输入到RNN模型中进行训练的问题。
利用图摘要技术加速模型训练和减少模型占用的计算资源。
technical_features_en: By introducing graph summarization technology to map the original graph to a fixed-size new graph, solving the problem that the output of the GNN model cannot be directly input into the RNN model for training.
Utilizing graph summarization technology to accelerate model training and reduce computational resource consumption.

novelty_points.claim: 提出了一种新的基于边分割的图流划分算法——Sketch-DBH，用于处理大规模图流数据下的子图划分问题。
novelty_points.claim_en: Proposed a new edge-segmentation-based graph stream partitioning algorithm - Sketch-DBH, for handling subgraph partitioning problems in large-scale graph stream data.
technical_features: 通过Count-Min Sketch这一概率数据结构存储每个节点的度数信息，并使用一个最小堆维护图流数据中的高频节点信息。
可以在常数时间内返回查询结果并据此生成单条图流数据即将被分配到的子图编号。
technical_features_en: Storing degree information of each node using Count-Min Sketch probabilistic data structure and maintaining high-frequency node information of graph stream data using a minimum heap.
Returning query results in constant time and generating the subgraph number for a single graph stream data to be allocated based on this information.

novelty_points.claim: 基于四个真实世界中的大规模时序图数据集进行了大量实验，与目前主流的动态图表示学习方法相比，GSAERU模型的训练速度更快，消耗内存更少，同时性能与目前最好的算法相比差距不超过3.5%。
novelty_points.claim_en: Extensive experiments on four real-world large-scale sequential graph datasets showed that the GSAERU model has faster training speed, less memory consumption, and performance comparable to the best-performing algorithms with a gap not exceeding 3.5%.

novelty_points.claim: 基于四个真实世界中的大规模图数据集，我们首先使用提出的DSGNN框架实现了三个经典图神经网络模型的分布式版本，并比较集中式与分布式训练下模型性能的差异。
novelty_points.claim_en: Based on four real-world large-scale graph datasets, we first implemented distributed versions of three classic GNN models using the proposed DSGNN framework and compared the performance differences between centralized and distributed training.
